note: Count<Derived>, Pixels and the empty RenderQuality -- the mutants that are decisive in the **Debug** tree. Its sibling m1-12-release.json holds the two that are decisive only where assertions are compiled out, and the reason for the split is the most useful thing the first run found. Count's wraparound guard has two halves: `if (wouldWrap) stopConstantEvaluation()`, a call to a function that is not constexpr, and `ORBSIM_EXPECTS(!wouldWrap)` beside it. **In Debug the second half does the first half's job as well**, because a failing assert is itself not a constant expression -- so mutating the marker function, or deleting the call to it, changes nothing a Debug build can see. Both survived here on 2026-09-23 against an expectation of 'caught', which is how this was found: the marker function's unique contribution exists only in the release tree, where the assert is gone. The run-time mutants are the mirror image and are only decisive here, where the assertion is live. Neither tree tests this code on its own.

mutants.name: the subtraction's condition is inverted, so it refuses what fits and allows what does not
the subtraction's condition is one off, and refuses a difference of exactly zero
mutants.why: Decisive only here. In the release tree the assertion is gone, the marker call does nothing at run time, and the subtraction goes on to give the right answer, so nothing would notice.

mutants.name: the addition's condition is inverted
mutants.find: const bool wouldWrap = other.value_ > kCountMaximum - value_;
mutants.replace: const bool wouldWrap = other.value_ < kCountMaximum - value_;

mutants.name: the addition's condition is one off, and refuses a sum that exactly fits
mutants.find: const bool wouldWrap = other.value_ > kCountMaximum - value_;
mutants.replace: const bool wouldWrap = other.value_ >= kCountMaximum - value_;
mutants.why: Decisive only here, for the reason the subtraction's one-off mutant gives.

mutants.name: the multiplication's condition is inverted
mutants.find: const bool wouldWrap = scale != 0U && value_ > kCountMaximum / scale;
mutants.replace: const bool wouldWrap = scale != 0U && value_ < kCountMaximum / scale;

mutants.name: the subtraction keeps only the compile-time half of its guard
mutants.replace:
const bool wouldWrap = other.value_ > value_;
        if (wouldWrap) stopConstantEvaluation();
mutants.why: It survives *this harness*, and does not survive the suite. The property is checked by the CTest entry count_wraparound_aborts, which this harness structurally cannot run: the probe's success is a non-zero exit -- the assertion firing -- and run_mutant reads any non-zero exit as a kill, so listing it here would report every mutant as caught. Removing the ORBSIM_EXPECTS makes the probe return 1 instead of aborting with 3, which cmake/VerifyCountWraparound.cmake calls a failure and this file cannot. Teaching mutate.py an inverted expectation would close the gap and is the owner's call, not this task's.
